_note: Autoterm heater fault codes, keyed by family then code. name is what the customer reads; vendor_name is Autoterm's own wording from their diagnostic tool; description is a Sensa draft for Autoterm to confirm; troubleshooting is an ordered list of steps supplied by Autoterm.

1.name: Overheat
1.description: The heat exchanger got too hot and the heater shut down to protect itself.

2.name: Possible overheat
2.description: The temperature readings suggest the heater is close to overheating.

5.name: Faulty temperature sensor
5.description: The heater's temperature sensor is giving a reading that cannot be right, or none at all.

6.name: Board temperature sensor fault
6.description: The temperature sensor on the heater's control board has failed.

9.name: Glow plug malfunction
9.description: The glow plug that lights the fuel is not working, so the heater cannot start.

10.name: Fan speed mismatch
10.description: The combustion fan is not turning at the speed the heater asked for.

12.name: Supply voltage too high
12.description: The heater's power supply voltage is above its safe limit.

13.name: No ignition
13.description: The heater tried to start but no flame was detected.

15.name: Supply voltage too low
15.description: The heater's power supply voltage is below what it needs to run.

16.name: Ventilation time exceeded
16.description: The heater could not cool down within the allowed purge time after stopping.

17.name: Faulty fuel pump
17.description: The fuel pump circuit is open or shorted, so no fuel is being delivered.

20.name: No connection
20.description: The heater and its controller have lost communication with each other.

27.name: Fan not turning
27.description: The combustion fan was told to run but is not turning.

28.name: Fan turning on its own
28.description: The combustion fan is turning when the heater has not told it to.

29.name: Flame goes out too often
29.description: The flame has gone out several times in a row while the heater was running.

30.name: No connection
30.description: The heater and its controller have lost communication with each other.

78.name: Flame went out while running
78.description: The flame went out while the heater was running.
